title: Follow a deeper question. | Joel student study

pages.text: HOSEA & JOEL / NOVEMBER 16–22, 2026
Follow a deeper question.
“I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.” Joel 2:28
Start with this week’s official Come, Follow Me lesson
OPTIONAL • About 5 minutes per module. Choose one or explore all four.
Begin with prayer. These readings extend the quick path rather than repeat it. Keep personal answers here or in your own notebook.
A / HOPE IN A TROUBLED WORLD
What kind of world receives this promise?
Make two short lists: What sounds frightening? What gives people reason to hope? The promise does not depend on the world becoming trouble-free first.
What difference could His presence and guidance make while your circumstances are still difficult?
B / A PROMISE ACROSS TIME
Was Joel’s prophecy fulfilled only once?
READ Joseph Smith—History 1:41
OPEN Scripture Helps: Hosea and Joel
Find the question about the Lord pouring out His Spirit upon all flesh. Follow its link to President Hinckley’s talk below.
READ “Living in the Fulness of Times” • President Gordon B. Hinckley
Read from “The era in which we live” through the paragraph about the restored priesthood. What examples does he connect with latter-day enlightenment?
Pentecost was a fulfillment, but not the whole story. How can a prophecy reach across more than one time?
HOSEA & JOEL / NOVEMBER 16–22, 2026
Different gifts. The same Lord.
Choose the question that interests you. You do not have to finish every module.
C / GIFTS WITHOUT COMPARISON
Does everyone receive the same gift?
READ Moroni 10:4–8, 17–18
Make two columns: What comes from the same source? What can differ between people? Notice how these verses connect spiritual knowledge and gifts with Christ.
Why is comparing experiences a poor way to decide whether God cares about you? What question about Jesus would you like to understand better?
D / PRACTICE SEEKING
How can I become more receptive?
READ Helaman 6:34–36
What attitudes are contrasted? Then read the paragraph beginning “In like manner, what will your seeking open for you?” and the next paragraph in:
“Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” • President Nelson
Choose a small practice: quiet time, honest prayer, scripture study, recording questions, or acting on something good you already understand.
I will try __________________ because…
Be patient. This is practice in seeking the Lord, not a test requiring an immediate feeling. Close with prayer.
